title: Visualizing Berry curvature in a Floquet-Chern insulator
authors: Younsik Kim, Rishi Acharya, Hannah E. Aguirre, Lucca Figari, Daniel P. Shoemaker, Fahad Mahmood
abstract: Circularly polarized light can open a topological gap in a gapless Dirac system, creating a Floquet-Chern insulator. However, its Berry curvature has not been directly resolved. Here we use circular-dichroism time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (Tr-ARPES) to map the light-induced Berry curvature of Floquet-Bloch states on the surface of Bi$_2$Se$_3$. By comparing spectra for opposite helicities of the mid-infrared pump, we isolate the induced geometric response. We observe alternating-sign Berry-curvature features at Floquet gaps that repeat at intervals set by the pump photon energy and redistribute with pump field strength in agreement with calculations for a periodically driven Dirac Hamiltonian. Both the induced Berry-curvature and the Floquet Dirac gap decay faster than the replica intensity, showing that spectral replicas can persist even after coherent Floquet hybridization weakens. These results establish momentum-resolved Berry-curvature mapping as a direct probe of light-induced topology and coherent Floquet band formation.
summary: This work uses time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy ($	ext{Tr-ARPES}$) to directly map the Berry curvature in a Floquet-Chern insulator on $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$. By exploiting the double-helicity dichroism signal, the authors demonstrate that the geometric response is sensitive to the driving field and evolves differently in time compared to the spectral replica intensity. This establishes a powerful experimental technique for probing light-induced topological properties.
main_problem: The primary goal is to directly measure and map the light-induced Berry curvature in a Floquet-Chern insulator state.
main_result: The study successfully mapped the Berry curvature using double-helicity dichroism, showing its systematic evolution with pump strength and distinguishing the driven topological state from static bands.
method: The measurement relies on circular-dichroism time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (Tr-ARPES) by comparing spectra taken with opposite pump helicities to isolate the geometric response.
model_or_system: The system is the surface of $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$, driven by mid-infrared circularly polarized light, which opens a topological gap and creates a Floquet-Chern insulator.
key_observables: Double-helicity dichroism signal, Berry curvature distribution ($\Omega$), Floquet-Bloch states, and the time-dependent gap splitting ($\Delta E_{split}$).
important_parameters: Pump photon energy ($\hbar\omega$), pump field strength (fluence), and time delay ($\Delta t$).
main_assumptions: The double-helicity dichroism method is assumed to isolate the pump-induced Berry curvature, and the temporal asymmetry is attributed to electronic heating and dephasing.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup, 2D curvature maps showing alternating-sign features, fluence dependence of dichroism, and temporal evolution showing strong asymmetry in the Berry curvature versus the replica intensity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for direct Berry curvature measurement to detailing the $	ext{Tr-ARPES}$ methodology, presenting results on periodicity and field dependence, and finally analyzing the time-resolved asymmetry between geometric response and spectral weight.
why_interesting: The technique provides a direct, momentum-resolved probe of Berry curvature induced by time-periodic driving, which is crucial for understanding light-matter interactions in topological materials and Floquet engineering.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Experimental schematic and double-helicity dichroism ARPES. (A) Schematic representation of a topological insulator and a Floquet-Chern insulator. Red and blue shading indicates the intensity of the induced Berry curvature. (B) Schematic of the time-resolved ARPES setup. (C) Conceptual illustration of circular dichroism angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) spectra and corresponding double-helicity dichroism signal near the Dirac point of a Floquet-Chern insulator.

FIG. 2. Floquet-induced gaps and double-helicity dichroism in a Floquet-Chern insulator. (A and C) Time- resolved ARPES (Tr-ARPES) spectra of Bi2Se3 acquired with a circularly polarized pump before pump arrival and at pump- probe temporal overlap, respectively. The pump fluence was 2.0 mJ/cm2. (B and D) Corresponding two-dimensional curvature maps. Black arrows in (D) indicate the Floquet-induced gaps. (E) Double-helicity dichroism spectrum corresponding to (C) (see Supplementary Materials [1] for the details of the double-helicity dichroism). (F) Energy distribution curve (EDC) of the double helicity dichroism spectrum, extracted from (E) at kx = 0.

FIG. 3. Fluence dependence of double-helicity dichro- ism and calculated Berry curvature. (A and B) Double- helicity dichroism spectra measured at pump fluences of 0.4 and 1.6 mJ/cm2, respectively. The dashed boxes labeled DP and AC indicate the regions used to evaluate the mean dichro- ism signals near the Dirac point and avoided crossing, respec- tively. (C and D) Calculated z-component Berry curvature distributions for peak drive fields of 1.6 × 107 V/m (corre- sponding to Floquet parameter β ≈0.13) and 3.2 × 107 V/m (β ≈0.26), respectively. (E) Ratio of the mean dichroism signals in the DP and AC regions, IDP/IAC, as a function of pump fluence.

FIG. 4. Temporal evolution of the Floquet-induced gap and double-helicity dichroism. (A) Tr-ARPES spectra as a function of time delay. (B) Corresponding double-helicity dichroism of A. Plots in B share the same color scale. (C) Energy distribution curves for Tr-ARPES spectra as a function of time near kx = 0. Grey shading indicates a single Lorentzian fit with a linear background, while red and blue shadings indicate a double Lorentzian fit. Red and blue triangles represent the peak positions for the double Lorentzian fit. (D) Peak separations as a function of time derived from the fits shown in C.
